note: Sources acquired after the Edition 1.1 cutoff and retained by Edition 1.2. Each is individually identified — one document ID, one role, one revision, one SHA-256 — rather than captured generically. A generic multi-document web capture can carry none of those and can never be manifested or resolver-selectable, which is why the seven pre-existing Louisiana multi-article browser prints are left untouched as non-workflow captures rather than promoted.

acquisitionGroups.basis: La. C.Cr.P. art. 986 provides that only the forms in Arts. 987 to 995 and 998 shall be used, so the forms are the text of the Code itself rather than judiciary-issued binaries. Each article is a distinct legislative act with its own amendment history and prescribes a functionally different document, so six article-specific sources are retained rather than one combined capture. The controlling source is the official HTML publication; no PDF was reconstructed from it.

acquisitionGroups.issuer: Iowa Judicial Branch; Maine Judicial Branch; Indiana Office of Judicial Administration
acquisitionGroups.basis: Official binaries acquired from the issuing authority for components Edition 1.1 did not manifest. Downloads that proved byte-identical to a copy already held or already retained were not re-imported; they were recorded as currentness confirmations against the existing asset instead. A third-party county mirror of the Montana MMRTA certificate of service was rejected: a secondary copy does not override an available official source, and that copy is itself marked unofficial.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 987 — Motion to set aside conviction and dismiss prosecution; rule to show cause; order of dismissal forms to be used
sources.notes: One article prescribing three forms: the motion to set aside the conviction and dismiss the prosecution, the rule to show cause, and the order of dismissal. Retrieved individually from the Louisiana State Legislature current-text publication on 2026-08-03. Source note at the end of the article: Acts 2014, No. 145, §1. Third-party blocks — the court's order of dismissal — are never participant-completed.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Re-read the article at the Legislature before any field-mapping work, because a statutory form changes by amendment rather than by revision stamp.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 988 — Motion for fee exemption form to be used
sources.notes: The article's official heading is "Motion for fee exemption form to be used"; the form it prescribes is captioned "CERTIFICATION OF FEE WAIVER" and directs that it be completed by the defendant, submitted to the District Attorney's Office before filing, and appended to the Motion for Expungement. Both names are correct and neither supersedes the other. Source note: Acts 2014, No. 145, §1; Acts 2015, No. 200, §1.
sources.requiredFollowUp: The district attorney's certification block is a third-party field and stays blank.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 989 — Motion for expungement forms to be used
sources.notes: The principal Louisiana petition. Form caption "MOTION FOR EXPUNGEMENT", opening with defendant information. The most-amended form in the set: Acts 2014, No. 145, §1; Acts 2015, No. 200, §1; Acts 2016, No. 125, §1, eff. May 19, 2016; Acts 2018, No. 711, §1; Acts 2020, No. 71, §1; Acts 2020, No. 73, §1.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Re-read the article at the Legislature before any field-mapping work; this article has been amended six times.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 991 — Order form to be used
sources.notes: The interim order, captioned "ORDER", which sets the district attorney's and arresting agency's sixty-day objection window and the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information's 120-day window. Judicial signature and date remain blank. Source note: Acts 2014, No. 145, §1.
sources.requiredFollowUp: The order is a proposed-order component; every judicial block stays blank.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 992 — Order of expungement form to be used
sources.notes: The final grant-or-deny order, captioned "ORDER OF EXPUNGEMENT OF ARREST/CONVICTION RECORD", including the redaction option. Art. 985.3(B) provides that only this form shall be used for court-ordered immediate expungement. The most recently amended article in the set: Acts 2014, No. 145; Acts 2015, No. 200; Acts 2016, No. 125, eff. May 19, 2016; Acts 2018, No. 711; Acts 2020, Nos. 71, 73 and 78; Acts 2024, No. 580.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Judicial findings, signature and date stay blank. Re-read before field mapping; amended as recently as the 2024 Regular Session.

sources.officialTitle: La. C.Cr.P. Art. 994 — Motion for interim expungement form to be used
sources.notes: Form caption "MOTION FOR INTERIM EXPUNGEMENT", the Art. 985.1 route for a felony arrest that resulted in a misdemeanour conviction. Source note: Acts 2014, No. 145, §1; Acts 2018, No. 711, §1.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Re-read the article at the Legislature before any field-mapping work.

sources.officialTitle: Application to Expunge Court Record (Iowa Code § 901C.2) — Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.86 Form 1
sources.notes: Iowa Judicial Branch published fillable form, January 2022 revision. This corrects a working assumption that the Rule 2.86 forms exist only as rule text: they are official standalone published forms.
sources.requiredFollowUp: None for source identity or currentness. Field mapping, rendering, legal-output and visual review remain.

sources.officialTitle: Application to Expunge Public Intoxication Records (Iowa Code § 123.46) — Iowa R. Crim. P. 2.86 Form 3
sources.notes: Iowa Judicial Branch published fillable form, January 2022 revision. An older July 2021 library entry exists and is superseded.
sources.requiredFollowUp: None for source identity or currentness.

sources.officialTitle: Order on Motion to Seal Criminal History for Victims of Sex Trafficking or Sexual Exploitation (Form CR-308)
sources.notes: Maine Judicial Branch form CR-308, Rev. 06/26. NARROW SCOPE: it is the order for a motion under 15 M.R.S. § 2262-B for victims of sex trafficking or sexual exploitation, created by LD 1871 effective 29 July 2026. It is NOT a generic proposed order paired with CR-218, and the Maine normalization treats it as though it filled the general ch. 310-A proposed-order gap. That conflict is recorded in the Edition 1.2 legal-design reconciliation queue and the affected track stays failed closed.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Resolve whether a general ch. 310-A proposed order exists; queue row e12-me-cr-308-scope.

sources.officialTitle: Form ACR — Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access

That conflict is recorded in the Edition 1.2 legal-design reconciliation queue.
sources.requiredFollowUp: Resolve the component document identity; queue row e12-in-form-acr-identity.
